why: Only a right-mover followed later by a left-mover can collide, and an incoming left-mover always hits the most recent surviving right-mover first. Survivors so far sit on a stack; each left-mover pops smaller right-movers off the top until it dies, ties, or passes everything.
hints: Which pairs can ever meet? And when a left-moving asteroid arrives, which surviving asteroid does it hit first?
It hits the nearest right-mover to its left, i.e. the top of a stack of survivors. Compare sizes: pop the top if it is smaller and keep going, pop both if equal, stop if the top is bigger.
Scan once; push right-movers, and process each left-mover against the stack top in a while loop; push it if it survives. Each asteroid is pushed and popped once, O(n).
pitfalls: Left-movers at the start (or after all right-movers are gone) never collide; push them.
Equal sizes destroy both: pop the top and drop the incoming asteroid.
A single left-mover can destroy several right-movers in a row: use a while loop, not an if.
